newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian govt to meet hard left over Stet.
newsitem.headline: Italian govt to meet hard left over Stet.

text.p: Government ministers will meet representatives from the hard-left Communist Refoundation shortly to try to break the stalemate over the sell-off of telecoms holding Stet, cabinet secretary Enrico Micheli said.

Refoundation, which guarantees the government's majority in the lower chamber of parliament, are ideologically opposed to the Stet privatisation and are effectively blocking key legislation concerning the planned sale.

"We don't plan to meet Refoundation today...but we will meet in the next few days," Micheli said. Prime Minister Romano Prodi met Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti to discuss Stet on Monday but their talks were inconclusive.
Refoundation has tabled numerous amendments to a government draft law which covers the creation of a watchdog body for the telecoms sector, seen as crucial to the privatisation.
The hard-right National Alliance has dropped its own amendments to the authorities bill, leaving Refoundation as the main obstacle to the legislation.
Asked if he thought an agreement could be reached, Micheli said: "I hope so".

The bill is due to go before the full Senate on November 11, 12 and 13. The government wants to privatise Stet by the end of March 1997 and commentators say that if the watchdog bill has not been ratified by year end the sell-off will be delayed. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
